title: Hardcoded px height with !important freezes on resize — use percentage that follows parent
trigger: Container height set via inline px + !important — element doesn't update when browser window resizes
principle: Inline px height with !important is a snapshot — it never updates on resize. Use height:100% so the element follows its parent's computed height automatically. The parent's height is set by the host page's CSS based on content/aspect-ratio and updates on resize without any JS listener.

cases.context: Split view wrapper inserted into host page DOM. Wrapper height set to parentPixelHeight px at insertion time. After browser resize, parent's computed height changes but wrapper stays at old px → empty space below video.
cases.good:
wrapper.style.cssText = `display:flex;height:100%!important;`;
// wrapper follows #container's computed height automatically on resize

cases.context: Video element sized via JS setSize(w, h) API — pixels set once, frozen on resize.
cases.bad: player.setSize(stageWidth, stageHeight); // frozen px, needs resize listener to update
cases.good:
// CSS: [data-cell-split-view="stage"] video{width:100%!important;height:100%!important;object-fit:contain!important}
// Video fills stage via CSS, adapts to resize automatically

applyFor: Video player containers in host pages
Any injected container that must match host element height
